question: What does 'shared decision-making' mean in nursing?

options.A: The patient deciding on treatments without any input from healthcare staff
options.B: The nurse making all clinical choices based solely on hospital policy
options.C: Family members making all health choices on behalf of the patient
options.D: Collaboration between the nurse and patient using clinical expertise and personal values

explanation: You got it! It's a true partnership where professional medical knowledge meets the patient's personal life values. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T6#GNS312_U4_T6_h7)

question: Which joint works just like a door hinge, letting you bend and straighten your elbow?

options.A: Condyloid joint
options.B: Saddle joint
options.C: Hinge joint
options.D: Pivot joint

explanation: Spot on! Hinge joints (like your elbow and knee) move back and forth smoothly in just one main direction. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why does a target cell undergo upregulation when hormone levels remain low for a long time?

options.A: To prepare the cell to stop functioning completely
options.B: To turn off the gene expression of the cell
options.C: To increase its sensitivity to the scarce hormone
options.D: To destroy excess hormone molecules in the blood

explanation: Adding more receptors helps the cell catch and respond to whatever small amount of hormone is available. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T9#GNS211_U1_T9_h5)

question: A patient with low iron levels eats plenty of beans and spinach. What advice should the nurse give to improve iron absorption?

options.A: Cook the vegetables in a microwave without water
options.B: Drink fresh orange juice or eat tomatoes with the meal
options.C: Drink a cup of strong black tea right after eating
options.D: Take the iron food with a glass of whole milk

explanation: Orange juice and tomatoes are rich in vitamin C, which enhances the absorption of non-heme iron found in plants. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which special opening connects the right atrium directly to the left atrium in a foetus?

options.A: Umbilical vein
options.B: Ductus venosus
options.C: Foramen ovale
options.D: Ductus arteriosus

explanation: Spot on! The foramen ovale is a clever little flap between the upper heart chambers that lets blood skip the right ventricle and lungs. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h2)

question: During a manual blood pressure check, what does the very first tapping sound (Korotkoff sound) tell you?

options.A: Systolic pressure
options.B: Venous return pressure
options.C: Mean arterial pressure
options.D: Diastolic pressure

explanation: Listen closely with your stethoscope! That first clear 'tap-tap' is the moment blood forces its way past the cuff as the peak systolic pressure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is a must-share piece of information during a patient handover?

options.A: The brand name of the hospital bed mattress
options.B: The patient's favorite television program
options.C: The personal phone number of the patient's relative
options.D: Current vital signs and recent lab results

explanation: Vitals and lab values give a clear, quick picture of how stable the patient is right now. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T5#GNS112_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which gastrostomy feeding method uses an electronic pump to deliver formula slowly over 24 hours?

options.A: Continuous feeding
options.B: Gravity drip feeding
options.C: Bolus feeding
options.D: Intermittent feeding

explanation: Continuous feeding runs at a slow, steady hourly rate throughout the day and night using a mechanical pump. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the best way to wash loose dirt and germs out of a fresh cut?

options.A: Soaking the entire wound in a tub of tap water
options.B: Scrubbing the inside of the cut with dry gauze
options.C: High-pressure irrigation using normal saline
options.D: Applying strong antiseptic solution directly into the tissue

explanation: Using a syringe with sterile saline creates just enough gentle pressure to wash away debris without harming the healing flesh. You're building great clinical skills! [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which germ causes oral thrush, also known as oral candidiasis?

options.A: Herpes simplex virus
options.B: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Candida albicans

explanation: Oral thrush is a fungal infection that happens when Candida albicans grows a bit too much in the mouth. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T4#GNS213_U3_T4_h2)

question: A nurse finishes drawing up an emergency medication from a single-dose vial. What should be done with the remaining liquid in the vial?

options.A: Save it in the pocket for the next patient
options.B: Put it back into the main supply drawer
options.C: Discard the leftover portion immediately
options.D: Leave the syringe attached for later use

explanation: Single-dose vials do not contain preservatives, so any leftover medication must be thrown away to prevent microbial growth. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical system-level cause of unsafe injections in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Heavy clinical workloads and lack of supervision
options.B: Strict enforcement of international sterilization policies
options.C: Severe shortages of disposable syringes and safety boxes
options.D: Proliferation of unregulated informal medicine vendors

explanation: Strict safety rules actually prevent unsafe practices! On the flip side, equipment shortages, busy staff, and unregistered drug sellers are major drivers of unsafe injections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why do nurses use the idea of a 'standard drink' instead of just counting glasses or bottles?

options.A: Serving sizes and alcohol strengths vary widely between different beverages
options.B: It makes tax calculations easier for local health authorities
options.C: Spirits contain no pure alcohol when mixed with water
options.D: Bottles of wine always contain exactly one standard serving

explanation: Not all drinks are poured equal! A big mug of stout packs way more punch than a small glass of wine. Using standard drinks helps patients track their real intake accurately. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T013#GNS227_U4_T013_h1)

question: What is the correct order for checking a patient's tummy during a physical exam?

options.A: Auscultation, inspection, palpation, percussion
options.B: Percussion, palpation, inspection, auscultation
options.C: Palpation, percussion, auscultation, inspection
options.D: Inspection, auscultation, percussion, palpation

explanation: You listen (auscultation) before you tap or press! If you touch the tummy first, you might change the natural bowel sounds and get a false reading. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h1)

question: What does a Doppler ultrasound check in a vascular patient?

options.A: Blood electrolyte and kidney filtration levels
options.B: Blood flow speed and whether vessels are open
options.C: Electrical heart rhythms
options.D: Bone strength and joint health

explanation: A Doppler ultrasound uses harmless sound waves to 'listen' to blood moving through vessels, helping us see if there are blockages or if blood is flowing backward. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T10#GNS213_U1_T10_h7)

question: During a home visit, the nurse sees loose scatter rugs on the floor. What is the best advice?

options.A: Recommend removing all loose rugs to prevent accidental slips and falls
options.B: Tape the edges of the rugs down securely with masking tape
options.C: Leave the rugs in place because they provide essential cushion
options.D: Instruct the patient to walk faster when crossing the rugs

explanation: You nailed it! Loose rugs are a major tripping hazard and should be cleared away for safety. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h8)

question: A nurse sighs loudly and makes a rude comment while cleaning up a PAC patient. Which nursing rule was broken?

options.A: Objective, non-judgmental communication
options.B: Aseptic surgical technique
options.C: Accurate medication dosage calculation
options.D: Emergency triage prioritization

explanation: Making disapproving remarks or sighs shames the patient and completely breaks the rule of giving non-judgmental, professional care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h3)

question: What is the proper thing to do with dirty bedsheets right after removing them from a patient's bed?

options.A: Fold them nicely and put them on the patient's bedside table
options.B: Place them directly into a designated laundry hamper
options.C: Drop them on the floor until you finish your shift
options.D: Spread them across a clean chair for later

explanation: Spot on! Putting dirty linens straight into the laundry basket stops germs from spreading around the ward and keeps tables clean. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T1#GNS112_U5_T1_h7)

question: Why is keeping strict confidentiality so important when young adults come for reproductive health services?

options.A: It speeds up the registration process in busy outpatient departments
options.B: It ensures the clinic receives extra funding from the government
options.C: It builds trust and encourages clients to seek care without fear of stigma
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to document patient interactions

explanation: Exactly! Young people especially worry about gossip. When they know their secrets are safe with you, they will gladly seek help without fear. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h3)

question: At what level of spinal cord injury does autonomic dysreflexia usually happen?

options.A: L1 or below
options.B: T6 or above
options.C: Any spinal injury
options.D: S1 to S5 only

explanation: Injuries at or above the sixth thoracic vertebra (T6) cut off communication between the brain and lower sympathetic nerves, risking this dangerous reflex. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h4)

question: Why must nurses specifically ask about herbal supplements during a medication history check?

options.A: Hospitals require patients to buy herbal tea during admission
options.B: Herbs can change how prescription drugs work in the body
options.C: Doctors use herbs to replace all standard intravenous fluids
options.D: Herbs are legally classified as Schedule I controlled substances

explanation: Herbal products can speed up or slow down drug metabolism, leading to unexpected treatment failures or toxicity. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h5)

question: What happens to the solid particles in a drug suspension over time?

options.A: Solid particles are dispersed and tend to settle
options.B: Solid particles are fully dissolved in the liquid
options.C: Active ingredients are bound permanently to the bottle
options.D: The mixture remains completely clear at all times

explanation: Think of muddy water! Suspensions have tiny bits of medicine floating around that love to sink to the bottom if left alone. That's why we always shake them first! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h1)

question: A patient feels a quick cramp during an endometrial biopsy in the clinic. What do you tell her?

options.A: Administer a full dose of general intravenous anesthesia immediately
options.B: Tell the patient that the procedure was performed incorrectly by the doctor
options.C: Call the emergency surgical team immediately for suspected uterine rupture
options.D: Explain that temporary uterine cramping is a normal response to tissue sampling

explanation: Well done! Passing tools through the cervix and taking a little tissue sample naturally causes brief, passing cramps. Reassuring your patient makes a huge difference. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the legal status of treating medical complications from an abortion in Nigeria?

options.A: It is strictly forbidden unless authorized by a high court judge
options.B: It is a legal and medically necessary life-saving intervention
options.C: It is classified as an elective cosmetic procedure
options.D: It is only permitted in federal tertiary teaching hospitals

explanation: Saving a patient's life by treating emergency complications is always legal and always the top priority in healthcare. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h4)

question: What is the first emergency medicine to give if a newborn's heart rate stays under 60 despite breathing support and chest compressions?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Sodium bicarbonate
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Epinephrine is our go-to emergency drug to help jumpstart the heart rate and improve heart muscle squeeze during severe bradycardia. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h6)

question: A patient arrives sweating heavily with thick makeup on their forehead. What should you do for their temperature?

options.A: Use the temporal thermometer right over the makeup
options.B: Use another route, like the ear or mouth
options.C: Wipe the forehead with alcohol and read immediately
options.D: Add two degrees to whatever the temporal reading says

explanation: Sweat and cosmetics mess up forehead heat readings. Save yourself a headache and switch to an oral or tympanic route! [learn more](GNS212_U4_T14#GNS212_U4_T14_h4)

question: During an EEG, the technician asks the client to breathe deeply and fast (hyperventilation). What happens in the body when you do this?

options.A: Build-up of lactic acid in the scalp muscles
options.B: Sudden expansion of fluid within brain ventricles
options.C: Increased oxygen levels and rapid heart deceleration
options.D: Decreased carbon dioxide and blood vessel constriction

explanation: Blowing off too much carbon dioxide makes your brain blood vessels tighten up a bit, which is a clever trick to help reveal hidden seizure activity on the screen. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h4)

question: Which of these items should go into the general, non-hazardous waste bin?

options.A: Empty cardboard boxes from IV fluid bottles
options.B: Used disposable injection syringes
options.C: An empty glass vial of chemotherapy drugs
options.D: Gauze soaked with a patient's blood

explanation: Spot on! Clean packaging hasn't touched body fluids or harsh drugs, so it's safe for the general bin. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h2)

question: What is the job of the air inlet on a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: It locks the cork lid tightly into the ceramic jar
options.B: It lets the nurse pour medicine in while treating
options.C: It acts as a drain for extra water collection
options.D: It allows fresh air to mix with the rising steam

explanation: Exactly! The air inlet lets a bit of cooler room air mix with the vapor. This keeps the steam from being too scorching hot for the patient's mouth and throat. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T6#GNS212_U2_T6_h2)

question: An Ebola patient is vomiting and having terrible watery diarrhea. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.A: Stop all oral meds until diarrhea clears up
options.B: Start aggressive rehydration therapy to correct fluid and electrolyte losses
options.C: Restrict all oral fluids to give the tummy a rest
options.D: Apply warm compresses to stop belly cramps

explanation: Spot on! Replacing lost fluids quickly is lifesaving because dehydration and shock are the big dangers here. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why is continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) often chosen over standard hemodialysis for critically ill patients?

options.A: It can be performed easily without any specialized equipment
options.B: It does not require any form of vascular access in the body
options.C: It completely cures chronic kidney disease within a few days
options.D: It removes fluids and toxins much more slowly and gently

explanation: CRRT filters blood continuously over 24 hours, making it much safer for hemodynamically unstable patients in the ICU. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the best bed position for a patient struggling to breathe who needs supplemental oxygen?

options.A: Prone position facing down on the bed
options.B: Semi-Fowler's or high-Fowler's position
options.C: Flat on the back with legs slightly raised
options.D: Trendelenburg position with tilted head

explanation: Sitting upright in Semi- or High-Fowler's position lets gravity help expand the lungs fully, making every breath much easier for your patient. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T9#GNS212_U2_T9_h3)

question: What is the biggest advantage of giving a client card directly to the patient to keep?

options.A: It saves the clinic money on buying storage cabinets
options.B: It prevents the clinic from ever writing anything down
options.C: It forces the patient to become a trained community health worker
options.D: The patient carries their health history with them to any new facility

explanation: Exactly right! Portable client cards ensure a patient's immunization and health history travels with them safely, even if they move away. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T13#GNS225_U2_T13_h5)

question: When giving a routine subcutaneous insulin injection to an adult, how should you position the skin and needle?

options.A: Inject the medication directly into the dermis until a fluid bleb forms.
options.B: Push the needle straight down into the muscle at a 90-degree angle.
options.C: Stretch the skin flat and insert the needle at a 15-degree angle.
options.D: Pinch a skin fold and insert the needle at a 45 to 90-degree angle.

explanation: You got it! Pinching the fatty tissue makes sure your needle stays in the fat layer and doesn't accidentally dive into the muscle underneath. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T15#GNS122_U1_T15_h4)

question: Why shouldn't you give an expectorant to someone with a dry, non-productive cough?

options.A: Dry coughs do not involve trapped mucus that needs loosening
options.B: Dry coughs always require strong narcotic suppression instead
options.C: It will permanently damage the delicate lining of the trachea
options.D: The medication will cause severe allergic reactions in the throat

explanation: You got it! Since there's no mucus present in a dry cough, an expectorant has nothing to work on and won't help the patient. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T3#GNS223_U2_T3_h1)

question: What should you do if a patient cannot speak because they have an endotracheal breathing tube in their throat?

options.A: Score the patient with a verbal score of 1 for total silence
options.B: Give the patient a verbal score of 5 assuming they are normal
options.C: Document the verbal score as untestable and note the breathing tube
options.D: Leave the verbal score section completely blank on the chart

explanation: Never guess! When a physical barrier like a breathing tube stops you from testing, clearly document why you couldn't check it so other nurses understand. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T7#GNS222_U3_T7_h7)

question: As a nurse, what is one of the best ways you can help stop drug resistance?

options.A: Administering broad-spectrum drugs for every common viral cold
options.B: Educating patients to finish their entire antibiotic prescription
options.C: Stopping medication immediately once mild symptoms disappear
options.D: Encouraging patients to save leftover pills for future sickness

explanation: You got it! Always remind patients to complete their meds. Stopping early leaves the toughest germs alive to breed stronger, resistant generations. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is your immediate nursing action right after the skin snip is taken?

options.A: Scrubbing the bleeding wound vigorously with soap
options.B: Applying direct pressure to the site until bleeding stops
options.C: Suturing the tiny wound closed with heavy nylon thread
options.D: Placing an ice pack directly on the open raw tissue

explanation: Correct! Simple direct pressure stops any minor bleeding at the tiny biopsy site before putting a bandage on. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T13#GNS213_U5_T13_h6)

question: What is the most reliable way to know how much pain a patient is feeling?

options.A: Changes in the patient's heart rate
options.B: The patient's own self-report
options.C: Family members' interpretation
options.D: The nurse's clinical observation

explanation: Exactly! Pain is whatever the patient says it is. Their personal word is always the gold standard for pain assessment. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T1#GNS123_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the main tool used by nurses during labor to track progress and detect complications early?

options.A: Glucometer
options.B: Partograph
options.C: Otoscope
options.D: Sphygmomanometer

explanation: The partograph is a graphic record of labor used to monitor maternal and fetal well-being and flag prolonged labor. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h4)

question: How does a community outbreak of food-borne illness usually begin?

options.A: From inherited family traits
options.B: From a shared contaminated food or water source
options.C: By direct physical contact at work
options.D: Through air droplets in crowded rooms

explanation: Spot on! When many people eat or drink from the same bad batch, it causes a community outbreak. You're building great clinical intuition! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T010#GNS227_U3_T010_h1)

question: What is a major financial barrier for families of special children in Nigeria?

options.A: Mandatory free private nursing care at home
options.B: Excessive government funding for all childhood treatments
options.C: Free international travel for medical checkups
options.D: High out-of-pocket costs for therapies and medical supplies

explanation: Most families bear the financial burden of care directly because public insurance coverage for chronic disabilities is limited. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h8)

question: Why is an unsafe injection a big deal in public health?

options.A: It almost always leads to immediate surgical site infections
options.B: It causes severe allergic reactions in every patient who receives it
options.C: It can easily transmit serious bloodborne infections to healthy individuals
options.D: It guarantees that the administered drug will not work properly

explanation: Unsafe practices bypass the skin's natural defenses, which can directly spread heavy infections like HIV and hepatitis into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h1)

question: What is the main tool used to see inside the tummy during a laparoscopy?

options.A: A handheld ultrasound scanner
options.B: A standard overhead operating lamp
options.C: An open surgical viewing mirror
options.D: A tiny camera called a laparoscope

explanation: You got this! A laparoscope is a thin, lighted tube with a tiny camera on the end. It sends clear pictures of the inside organs to a TV monitor for the surgeon. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the difference between a salpingostomy and a salpingectomy?

options.A: Salpingostomy uses medication to dissolve tissue, whereas salpingectomy uses a laser to clear blockages
options.B: Salpingostomy repairs a ruptured tube, whereas salpingectomy prevents future infections
options.C: Salpingostomy removes the pregnancy while keeping the tube, whereas salpingectomy removes the tube entirely
options.D: Salpingostomy is done for uterine pregnancies, whereas salpingectomy is done for ovarian implantations

explanation: A salpingostomy opens the tube to remove the pregnancy tissue, saving the tube, whereas a salpingectomy removes the affected fallopian tube completely. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h6)

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation in nursing care?

options.A: To completely cure chronic underlying pathologies
options.B: To eliminate the need for any follow-up care
options.C: To maximize a person's independence and functional level
options.D: To keep patients admitted in hospital wards long-term

explanation: You've got this! Rehab is all about helping your patients live life to the fullest and do as much for themselves as possible, even if a chronic condition is still there. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T6#GNS123_U6_T6_h1)

question: What do we call the solid ball of about 16 cells formed in the first few days after fertilization?

options.A: Zygote
options.B: Blastocyst
options.C: Morula
options.D: Trophoblast

explanation: Great job! After a few cell divisions, this little cluster of cells looks just like a tiny mulberry, which is why it's named the morula. Learning embryology step by step is easier than you think! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T005#GNS226_U2_T005_h1)

question: A client wants to use the rhythm method, but her husband refuses to help or participate in cycle tracking. What should you do?

options.A: Refuse to provide any further healthcare services at the clinic
options.B: Tell her to force her husband to read the calendar against his will
options.C: Sign her up for the rhythm method anyway without mentioning her husband
options.D: Counsel the client on the need for partner cooperation and discuss alternative methods she can control independently

explanation: Methods like rhythm and withdrawal take teamwork. If her partner isn't on board, guide her toward choices she can manage completely on her own, like injectables or implants. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h8)

question: Why is it so helpful to introduce psychological support early after a degenerative diagnosis?

options.A: It helps patients adapt before severe cognitive decline sets in
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future medical interventions
options.C: It stops the physical degeneration from spreading to organs
options.D: It guarantees complete recovery from emotional distress

explanation: Starting early means patients can still clearly express their thoughts and take part in planning their own care. Great nursing insight to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T18#GNS222_U4_T18_h1)

question: What is spermatogenesis?

options.A: The release of seminal fluid during ejaculation
options.B: The storage of mature sperm inside the epididymis
options.C: The hormonal control of secondary sex characteristics
options.D: The production of mature sperm cells from primitive germ cells

explanation: Spermatogenesis describes the biological creation and development of mature sperm cells from immature precursors in the testes. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h1)

question: In which direction should you smooth a topical lotion onto a patient's skin?

options.A: Strictly from the bottom of the limb upward
options.B: In a crisscross pattern across the rash
options.C: In the direction of hair growth
options.D: In tight circular motions against the hair

explanation: Smoothing lotions in the direction of hair growth keeps hair follicles happy and prevents painful inflammation. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T20#GNS122_U1_T20_h7)

question: What happens to the body during activation of the sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Digestion speeds up to process recent meals
options.B: Heart rate increases and airways dilate for quick action
options.C: Pupils constrict to focus on close objects
options.D: Blood flow is directed entirely to the stomach

explanation: The sympathetic division prepares the body for stressful or emergency situations by boosting alertness and physical readiness. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is yellow jaundice showing up in the first 24 hours of life a worry for nurses?

options.A: It indicates that the mother is breastfeeding too frequently
options.B: It is a normal physiological process seen in all preterm babies
options.C: It shows that the infant is experiencing acute dehydration
options.D: It points to pathological processes like blood group incompatibility

explanation: Jaundice on day one is never normal. While regular newborn jaundice can show up later, early jaundice usually means something serious like blood type mismatch or liver trouble. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h6)

question: Why does a heart wall rupture quickly lead to pulseless electrical activity (PEA)?

options.A: The coronary arteries experience massive spasms that stop electrical impulses.
options.B: The brain receives signals to shut down the heart completely.
options.C: The electrical system stops working because the heart muscle dies.
options.D: Blood escapes completely out of the heart chambers, leaving no volume to pump.

explanation: When the heart wall tears, blood pours out into the chest. The electrical sparks might keep firing for a bit, but with no blood left inside to pump, you get PEA. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T9#GNS213_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which embryonic germ layer gives rise to the nervous system and skin?

options.A: Trophoblast
options.B: Mesoderm
options.C: Ectoderm
options.D: Endoderm

explanation: Think 'ecto' for outer—the outer layer builds things that face the outside world, like your skin and your brain/nerves! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which of these actions is a dangerous nursing practice that you must strictly avoid after giving an injection?

options.A: Engaging built-in safety shields
options.B: Throwing away syringes immediately
options.C: Using a sharps container
options.D: Recapping used needles by hand

explanation: Spot on! Trying to recap needles by hand is a major cause of accidental needle-stick injuries. Never do it! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T7#GNS122_U1_T7_h6)

question: How does the cerebellum use an 'efference copy' during a voluntary movement?

options.A: To produce neurotransmitters required for neuromuscular transmission
options.B: To directly contract skeletal muscles without involving the cortex
options.C: To store long-term procedural memories of past movements
options.D: To compare intended motor commands with actual sensory feedback

explanation: An efference copy is like a duplicate draft of the brain's movement plan sent to the cerebellum so it can check: 'Did our body actually do what we wanted it to do?' Brilliant nursing brain at work! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T22#GNS211_U3_T22_h4)

question: What does the term 'caregiver burden' usually mean in clinical practice?

options.A: The paperwork required by insurance companies for blood products
options.B: The financial cost charged by the hospital for daily inpatient admission
options.C: The physical and emotional strain experienced by family members providing care
options.D: The legal responsibility nurses hold for medication administration errors

explanation: Family caregivers often pour all their energy into the patient and forget themselves, leading to deep fatigue and burnout. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T4#GNS311_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the maximum score for the verbal (talking) category in a fully alert adult?

question: Why is it so important to check lab results alongside a physical assessment rather than trusting the numbers alone?

question: Where is the median cubital vein located, which is a favourite spot for starting an IV?

question: Why is it smart to check inside a patient's mouth with a penlight after they finish a meal?

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation nursing compared to regular hospital care?

question: Why is wearing loose cotton clothing a great tip for patients with skin issues in hot, humid weather?

question: What does agenda setting mean in health policy?

question: Why do public health organizations strongly support male circumcision in many regions?

question: How does a typical resting tremor look in a patient with early Parkinson's disease?

question: What is a major risk when using large amounts of plain tap water for a washout?

question: When is the best time to encourage a patient to attempt bowel evacuation during a training program?

question: How does a hormonal IUD locally affect the uterus to help prevent pregnancy?

question: Even if a bandage or gown looks completely dry, why should you still treat it as an infection risk?

question: How does a hemorrhagic stroke cause damage to the brain?

question: Which type of cardiomyopathy involves abnormal thickening of the heart muscle walls?

question: What is the primary goal of Post-Abortion Care (PAC) services?

question: What is the main job of the aqueous humor in the eye?

question: What is an essential safety habit after calculating a children's drug dose?

question: Why might someone having a severe gout attack still have a normal blood uric acid level?

question: As a nurse, what is one of your main duties when it comes to environmental health?

question: Why is good etiquette especially important when nursing inside a patient's home?

question: Why is family planning so important for mothers' health in Nigeria?

question: Why does a woman with an infibulated scar have a higher risk of prolonged labor?

question: What tough, fibrous layer of connective tissue tightly wraps around the corpora cavernosa to give it support?

question: After teaching a patient about wound care, what must the nurse document in the patient's notes?

question: What is a key sleep tip you can teach a patient who is getting ready for discharge?

question: What type of cells make up the inner part of the adrenal gland (adrenal medulla), and where do they come from?

question: When is home quarantine most appropriate to use during an outbreak?
